The zoom gesture is the same everywhere, and the page strip names the page you are on. More at [www.malgel.com](https://www.malgel.com).

## Fixed

- **The wheel means the same thing on every surface.** Command or Control plus the wheel zooms the editor, the preview, the image viewer, the diagram window and the PDF viewer; the wheel on its own scrolls, or moves the diagram. Before, the bare wheel zoomed the image and diagram viewers while the PDF viewer and the editor wanted a modifier, so the same gesture did two different things depending on where the pointer was. A zoomed-in image can now be scrolled with the wheel too, which it could not be before.
- **The PDF page strip highlights the page you are on.** The strip's current-page mark was written while the pages were being drawn, so it could name a different page than the toolbar beside it; both now read the page from the scroll position before either is drawn.

Both are part of the pass over the small interactions that 0.1.7 began with drag-to-move — the wheel, clicks and drags, checked one by one against what VS Code does with the same gesture.

## Downloads

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| macOS 11+ (Apple silicon) | `Malgel-0.1.8-macos-arm64.dmg`: open it and drag Malgel to Applications |
| Windows 10+ | `Malgel-0.1.8-windows-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `Malgel-0.1.8-windows-x64.zip` (portable) |
| Linux x86_64 | `Malgel-0.1.8-x86_64.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it, then run it) or `malgel-0.1.8-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |

The macOS app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so Gatekeeper blocks it after download: right-click it and choose Open once, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Malgel.app`. The Windows files are unsigned: SmartScreen may warn, and **More info → Run anyway** gets past it. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists every file's checksum.
